## APK installation outcome · 2026-11-16

Installation failure was reported without a specific system error. The device failure has not been reproduced or diagnosed. Static inspection of official 0.1.306 and 0.1.315 APKs found matching certificates/package IDs, increasing version codes, ARM64 libraries and verified v2 signatures/content digests. This is not phone-installation acceptance.

- APK-INSTALL-01: Keep the signed manifest, full-file length/hash, package/version/certificate validation and unknown-source permission handoff. Copy the verified APK into a PackageInstaller session, fsync it, and retain the download and existing user data on failure. Never uninstall or change signing identity as a speculative remedy. Equal version codes report already installed; a lower candidate reports downgrade blocked, without relaxing the strict upgrade or certificate check.
- APK-INSTALL-02: Commit only after the user's Install action; require system user confirmation. A non-exported receiver persists the system result without launching UI. Its mutable status PendingIntent is bound to one session/token and only handed to PackageInstaller. A separate explicit immutable one-shot confirmation PendingIntent is consumed only by the RESUMED status activity or a user notification tap; no background-launch-always grant. Without notification permission, the manager strongly retains the pending confirmation for this process. Process death or a missing OS-held confirmation is not promised recoverable: the screen explicitly offers cancel-this-session/retry. An older unfinished version opens an explicit recovery choice before any new-version install; it is never silently replaced or confirmed.
- APK-INSTALL-03: Accept callbacks only for the persisted session/token and matching system session ID. Session publication and identity-checked receipt mutations share one lock; APK staging and fsync stay outside it. Cancellation targets only the captured session and rechecks identity before recording its result. Terminal results are monotonic, with actual installed-version evidence taking precedence. Persist and display real status/detail, distinguish success, abort (user cancellation or system abort), conflict, invalid/incompatible package, storage and policy failures. Missing callbacks and failed UI handoffs remain unknown. Repeated taps reuse the owned session instead of creating duplicate installs; sealed sessions wait for the original result or offer an explicit cancel-this-request confirmation before retrying. Abandon only the owned staging session, never the installed app or downloaded APK. Persistence failures are disclosed and retain session ownership.
- APK-INSTALL-04: Keep receipt text across reopening/checking for the matching version and reconcile actual installed version after self-update process replacement. Do not equate UI launch, CI success or static APK checks with successful installation on the user's phone. The first update from an older app still uses that older install path; this new receipt path is available only after a version containing it has been installed.

Reference contracts: `developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller.Session`, `developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller`, `developer.android.com/reference/android/app/ActivityOptions`. Verification here is source review only: no local test/build, emulator or device install was run. Original failure root cause and device lifecycle behavior remain unverified.


## Reader readiness count stability · 2026-11-17 (READCOUNT-01–05)

User report (message `Sentinel_439935cb67b08191979386df5d9c880e`): “关于那个看漫画的时候那个关于体验策略那个栏呢，有bug，就是显示当前阅读了多少个嘛，那个我先配置是16，16。翻页的时候它总是会跳，你知道吗？有时候跳到一，有时候跳到二。它这个会跳啊，它不稳定啊。这肯定是你前端或者什么逻辑的bug啊”. No screenshot or device trace accompanies this report; the precise field and device trigger remain unconfirmed.

- READCOUNT-01: Keep the configured forward/review counts and actual current-window original readiness distinct. Never force the measured count to 16. A partially inspected window displays a `?` and discloses the unknown count; no complete-readiness progress bar is inferred from partial evidence.
- READCOUNT-02: Layout settling, image remeasurement and restoration cannot reverse reading direction and cancel its work. Vertical readers derive direction from consumed scrolling or an explicit navigation target; internal restore/resize positioning does not change it, and overlapping navigation keeps suppression ownership until every operation settles. Paged readers retain their existing anchor-turn behavior. Primary and standby preparation share the same reader direction. True reverse reading retains its existing behavior; fractional position still informs speed estimation.
- READCOUNT-03: Separate target-window observation/finished-resource retention from optional-work admission. The new visible page loading can pause work but cannot discard overlapping completed-resource identities. Keep real cancellation, byte limits, foreground promotion and existing cache owners.
  - If a download takes ownership between initial resolution and script/JM preparation, defer and recheck its local ownership at the existing retry interval. Missing downloaded bytes must not permanently mark the original finished, bypass the download's route, launch a duplicate transfer, or consume source-failure retries. Only this explicit local-ownership outcome is retryable; an unsupported provider's generic null result is not. This is a statically identified race path, not a confirmed diagnosis of the user's device.
- READCOUNT-04: Freshness follows the configured sampling interval and observed scan duration, not an unrelated fixed four-second timeout. Observations still expire to unknown. Same-tracker layout restarts retire owned activity without erasing recent exact-page artifact checks; stale effect owners cannot publish artifacts into a replacement owner.

- READCOUNT-05: A `PrefetchBudgetExceeded` outcome belongs to the concrete byte-window owner captured by its attempt. A later window with usable remaining bytes may retry that still-targeted page only after its old request settles. Do not wait for unrelated configuration changes, retry repeatedly within the same exhausted window, reset real source-failure retry limits or move in-flight charges to a new budget. This repairs a source-confirmed stop path: old `originalFinished` survived window renewal while the recovery key did not include the actual byte-window owner. It does not establish that this was the phone screenshot's cache-write gate.

Cache-pause wording now says “等待可回收空间；当前阅读和下载受保护”, rather than promising that waiting restores capacity. The existing Cache scope and experience-settings action remain the inspection/capacity-adjustment entries; this does not change the cache owner or establish that protected data caused the reported pause.

Source evidence at main `3e627f7`: the pager supplies fractional offsets; the collector previously used every delta sign as a direction change. `visibleReady=false` emptied `desired`, which also pruned completed resource maps. The tracker expired every artifact after four seconds although cache observation has a user-configurable interval and serial local inspections. These are source-confirmed mechanisms consistent with count drops, not a reproduction of the user's phone. The patch preserves existing READBAR/STATUSCOLOR controls, ownership and manual values. Source/diff review only; no tests, local builds, probes or UI automation. Installed behavior remains pending user feedback.

The first viewport answers current usage and the effect of the draft, then exposes one selected setting category. Neutral base surfaces preserve reading context; accent denotes selection, amber denotes actual pressure/pending trim, and error color denotes a failed operation. Automatic resource adaptation applies only to automatic settings, preserving explicit user values and honest operational failures.

The recovery surface uses the existing reader panel/thumbnail/button grammar. Catalogue alignment and page equivalence are separate concepts. Long-lived exact mappings are fenced by work, logical chapter, both native manifests and source identities.

### UI/UX design decisions and reuse

The core journey is discovery/search → work detail → source preview → confirm season/line → select episode → watch → return/continue → review tracking differences. The shared navigation and compact anime header retain the existing glass/motion family; content stays clear and content-led. The source workspace discloses candidate search, bound catalogues and per-episode correction in that order. Tracking comparison is a separate context, so a playback-line mismatch cannot masquerade as a cloud-progress conflict.

The implementation reuses the repository's actual MotionTabs, press buttons, sliders, retained panels/popovers, title header, source-mark and search foundations. It does not introduce an alternate component system or assert that generic Material defaults satisfy the user's UI preference. Sources are adapted from the existing project components and the references already documented below; no invented screenshot stands in for an installed UI.

- Adopt current provider contracts from KazumiRules (MIT) and the cited AGE adapter, preserving exact source identity; the installed rules do not establish present availability.
- Adapt Bangumi's actual episode collections API and AniList's GraphQL model; preserve their different expressive power instead of flattening both to a guessed episode count.
- Combine an app-owned session controller with native playback engines and existing routed networking/cache ownership. Do not reuse the wallpaper MediaPlayer as the full player.

Retained reader callbacks require their actual active session. A native prefetched request carries its exact body observer into the visible attempt, ignoring pre-visibility/other-page data and preserving the last real progress at handoff; continuous positive bytes no longer expire solely because prefetch owned the network request. A late failed preflight latches one exact-attempt cache bypass, and manual retries keep bypassing a suspect original until a positive-dimension foreground network decode succeeds, without evicting a concurrent replacement or replaying success. Cache-only validation does not count as its own prefetch benefit. A queued disk-cache growth can continue optional work in the existing applied LRU while leases settle; shrink/zero/error/closed states still block it and there remains one journal owner.

## Unified experience, network and download delivery · 2026-11-14 (TRANSFER-195–204)

User explicitly supplied the full “MangaFlow 核心体验系统 · 深度重构设计” and requested “需要你完全把它落地子代理开起来” (current conversation, exact message ID unavailable). | ID | Implementation contract and observable acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| TRANSFER-195 | One generation-bound runtime progress model separates received/retained partial bytes, actual newly transferred bytes, verified completed pages and verified saved bytes. Publish at bounded intervals rather than per chunk to disk. A known current page length permits that page's byte ratio only; unknown chapter bytes never produce an invented chapter percentage. Speed uses actual byte/time samples and expires when no data arrives. |
| TRANSFER-196 | Each active page has connecting, first-byte, receiving, verification and commit phases. Admission waiting has a named reason and a bounded worker lifetime. On resource deferral, stop admitting new pages, allow already-started siblings to settle safely, persist waiting and release the platform worker. Retry times and actual failure classes survive the durable queue; resource waits do not consume the finite network-failure budget. |
| TRANSFER-197 | Current visible pages retain their independent permit; reading restricts new background work without cancelling receiving pages. Ordinary, paged and guided readers observe only their exact page/request and attempt-owned Coil/script byte observer. Their45second foreground deadline measures lack of positive body progress; headers, cache hits, other pages and stale/cancelled attempts cannot renew it. Unknown sources begin at one request, grow only after real stable successes, contract on failures and retain the longest advertised 429/503 cooldown. Chapter/page tickets remain fair; disk protection has recovery headroom. Existing cache leases, manual ceilings and original-byte budgets stay owned by their existing controllers. |
| TRANSFER-198 | Freeze a task route before metadata preparation and reuse it through source resolution, redirects and image saving. Default retry uses that saved route; a separate explicit action adopts current category/global settings. The distinction also covers source-refresh and failed preparation. Later settings changes cannot silently change a running task or force a proxy task to direct. Valid offline pages remain readable. |
| TRANSFER-199 | Page streaming has independent response/first-data and inactivity deadlines plus a generous whole-call safety bound. This applies to the actual Ktor download, JVM/iOS script-image transports and the shared Coil factory; iOS script progress excludes HTTP headers and chunk framing. Native decrypted transports without a streaming callback retain honest phase-only observations. Script images retain their existing bounded materialization cache rather than falsely claiming HTTP Range support. Continuous positive byte progress must not be killed by the ordinary API timeout. Strong ETag, If-Range, exact 206/416 validation, identity-sensitive partials, original-image verification and atomic commits remain authoritative. TLS, DNS, connection, authorization, rate limiting, source expiry, validation and storage failures stay distinct. |
| TRANSFER-200 | Reuse existing DownloadBookRow, compact retained PANEL, Ovio/MotionTabs, beUI press, MotionSwap and SettingsDisclosure. Keep the existing 4dp row padding/2dp separators and scrolling ownership. Primary metadata shows saved pages and the actual current stage/bytes; detail is disclosed from the existing metadata area, not a new permanent action column or large card. Only the current page's known byte ratio owns the fine progress line. Retry actions explicitly name original versus current-settings route. |
| TRANSFER-201 | Network retains Connection / By type / Check and one scene-height owner. Detected device configuration, defaults for new work and the running task's frozen route remain different facts. Experience mode stays first, with a compact actual capacity/protection explanation and target-versus-effective values inside each existing disclosure. Preserve retained exit/reversal, keyboard/viewport behavior, reduced motion and 44dp controls. Installed smoothness and large-font layout remain unverified until user feedback. |
| TRANSFER-202 | Android notifications consume the same real progress state at a slower cadence. Android 14+ user-initiated foreground scheduling may use UIDT through the same chapter execution engine; recovery/unsupported launch retains WorkManager and exact work ownership. Windows restores the durable queue when the process restarts. iOS uses its actual finite native execution lease and restores on return; do not claim every script/decrypted image can run in a background URLSession or continue after force quit. Native constraints must be visible near the existing background preference. |
| TRANSFER-203 | Explicit connection checks retain actual HTTP status, failure class, total attempt duration, sample count and advertised retry deadline. No guessed DNS/TLS timing or bandwidth claim. Copy/export uses an allowlist report omitting URLs, proxy endpoints, identities, headers and raw exception chains. Opening settings must not initiate active connectivity probes. |
| TRANSFER-204 | Root owns final integration and publication, preserving latest main, one complete source batch and ordinary CI activation. Follow the current no-tests/no-local-build/no-service-or-device-probe workflow. Source review is not compilation, installed visual acceptance or measured performance. The RFC's real device acceptance matrix remains pending user installation; record concrete platform limitations rather than treating unobserved cases as passed. |

That consumes scroll as well as unsafe mutations. Remove only that grid gate and allow its pure preview callbacks/press feedback. Browsing a different preview never cancels or replaces the active task. Actual phone feel remains pending. |
| Download preparation route / P0 OPEN | MangaViewModel2613–2616 fetches repository.pages before downloads.enqueue; needsSourceRefresh retry2242 has the same path. CHAPTERS snapshot is captured only later in DownloadStore.beginTransfer. Copy SourceHttp, JS getPageList and old JM pages therefore can contact the original route before the routed worker exists. This is a real code-level coverage gap, not a live endpoint reproduction. The next bounded slice should acquire one route before preparation, isolate preparation requests/sharing by that route, and persist the same snapshot into enqueue/refresh. Keep ordinary reading/browsing/auth unchanged. Merely adding coroutine context without route-scoped in-flight identity is insufficient: UnifiedMangaRepository779–798 and CopyMangaRepository284–298 merge by chapter only. |
| Legacy Steam progress / P0 OPEN | Actual pinned session.rs Legacy branch awaits Fetch::get into one complete Response.body, checks its size and only then writes FileSink. Native adapter initially emits0/total and emits completion afterwards; Legacy has no intermediate Event::Progress. Thus the progress bar can remain at0 even while bytes arrive. The payload bound512MiB is not a constant-memory guarantee. Next adapt the maintained fetch/body path to bounded streaming into the owned file with real byte progress, preserving route/TLS/cancel/path/media limits. Do not fake progress with a timer. |
| Task scope / P1 OPEN | Current visible controls configure subsequent category defaults, not one task's independent override or the actual currently connected route. Make one-off vs saved-default scope explicit and display a task's frozen choice separately from future defaults. The optional snapshot override API alone is not a user-facing task picker. |

## Download routing implementation · 2026-11-14 (DOWNLOAD-ROUTING-143)

This implements ROUTING-DESIGN-142 after the user's “继续”; the intervening “失败了” report was independently diagnosed from actual workflow logs. Keep the raw full requirement and Steam UI/authentication decisions in STEAM-UI-141. Scope is download connection selection and its UI; ordinary reading/source browsing/auth retain their prior transports, except Steam's explicitly labelled connection setting which intentionally includes its own authentication/search/CDN job.

### Current adopted behavior and actual UI

- Settings → 应用 → 网络与下载 owns the default download mode, one explicit proxy endpoint, and progressive independent category defaults. Existing Ovio MotionTabs, Motion buttons, quiet input rows and retained MotionDialog/PANEL paths are reused. Explicitly available Haze sources keep the panel material; absent sources retain the normal existing Surface fallback.
- System network / app direct / specified proxy are different modes. Category controls can inherit; a task captures its effective route at start. The shared snapshot API additionally accepts an optional overrideMode; current visible controls configure the category default for subsequent tasks, not an invented per-running-task live switch. Download UI, fonts, models, runtime, Steam, update, WebDAV and source-import entry points expose the appropriate compact control; ongoing tasks disable their local setting control.
- “应用直连” means no app/system HTTP or SOCKS proxy for this transfer, not a guarantee to bypass another VPN, TUN or router. No whole-process network binding, global ProxySelector/env mutation, new VPN or fake bypass toggle is introduced.
- New proxy setup defaults to SOCKS5 because it supports more actual download paths. Endpoint accepts validated host/IP, port and HTTP/SOCKS type; no username/password, URL credentials or guessed working port. Missing or unsupported configuration produces a concrete error before a request. Proxy failures do not silently switch direct.
- Defaults affect new tasks and explicit manual retry. Existing chapter work IDs preserve their saved snapshot across automatic retry/restart; explicit retry cancels/joins the previous generation before using new settings. Metadata added to the existing manifest is optional and backward compatible, carries no credentials and is validated. Damaged optional routing never downgrades a completed chapter or discards files.
- A conditional setup remains possible where the external client supports both per-app exclusion and a local listener: exclude MangaFlow from that VPN/TUN capture, enter its local SOCKS/HTTP listener, and route selected downloads explicitly to it. Ordinary source browsing/reading still use their prior network and must remain reachable in such a setup; this is not automatic or universally verified bypass.

| Download route | Actual source implementation / ownership |
| --- | --- |
| Shared HTTP | DownloadRoutingStore persists application download/category defaults. NetworkClient holds one checked immutable snapshot. Android/desktop configure the actual OkHttp builder; DIRECT explicitly uses NO_PROXY. iOS configures actual SOCKS/session behavior. No route parameter preserves prior reader/auth behavior. |
| Normal chapters | The worker owns one routed NetworkClient, passes it through DownloadStore to DownloadPageTransfer, and closes it through endTransfer. Preserve current acceptCompression=false, response headers, strong ETag/Range,2 mobile/4 desktop workers, original source/page identity and persisted progress. |
| JM chapters | A chapter-owned JmDownloadSession uses the pinned5a7a4bb/v1.1.12 public configuration/context/JmApiClient constructor. Its actual HTTP client carries the route through initialization probes, settings, metadata and decoded media. Keep upstream cookie/domain/TLS/decoding behavior; reader's existing client remains unchanged. Do not set domainProbeIntervalMs(0): the real implementation schedules it without a zero guard. |
| Fonts and AI models | Each started transfer constructs its routed client within the task try/finally. Preserve manifests, verified payload/hash, cancellation, licensing and complete original font/model data. Do not freeze defaults when the store is first created. |
| Android runtime / Steam component | Each actual component transfer owns an isolated routed OkHttp client. Catalogue, archive, redirects and cancellation retain the same snapshot. Steam uses STEAM_COMPONENT, other runtime engines COMPONENTS. Original signer, version, ELF and SHA checks remain. |
| Application updates | Android HttpURLConnection check/download redirects and Range use a task-local Proxy. NonAndroid full updates own routed Ktor clients; desktop incremental manifest and Update4j streams receive the same snapshot, including a fallback to the complete package. Keep source/current-main/tag/signing/hash and platform installer guards. |
| Third-party source installation | Preserve original NO_PROXY/public DNS/IP checks and original URL Host/TLS/SNI. A bounded SOCKS SocketFactory accepts only an already-resolved verified public target IP; Android sends that numerical address to SOCKS, preventing independent proxy-side DNS from bypassing validation. HTTP proxy is explicitly unsupported here. JS browsing/auth APIs stay on their prior path; their original image downloads use CHAPTERS. Local files need no new network transfer. |

These paths fail explicitly, rather than displaying success or falling back unasked.

| Budget | 节能 candidate | 自动 candidate | 流畅优先 candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background pages | mobile1 /desktop2 | start mobile2 /desktop4, adjust slowly from actual outcomes | ceiling mobile4 /desktop8 subject to safety limits |
| Neighbor prefetch | ahead1 /behind0 | total1–4, direction and visible waiting decide | total4–8 within byte/memory budget |
| Native region decode |1 | desktop2 /iOS1; Android native Telephoto | retain these initial caps until actual evidence supports change |
| Refresh hint | release sustained peak preference; system touch boost remains | High for interaction/scroll; no idle redraw loop | High preference with native display synchronization |
| Cache | smaller initialization budget | actual process budget and free storage | higher user ceiling with protected download/system headroom |

Controller contract: current-page loading never waits for sensing or a speed test. Learn only from real uncached request bytes/time, first-byte wait, cache hits and decode/current-page readiness; each source owns its own congestion/backoff. Unknown paths, including a native source without these measurements, keep conservative defaults. Increase one lane only after stable healthy observations;429/503, repeated timeouts, memory pressure or serious heat reduce optional admissions first. Change only future admissions; never replace an in-use Semaphore, restart a visible image or invalidate an in-flight file because a profile changes. Disk pressure evicts only rebuildable cache and stops speculative work; imported books, offline chapters, exact download checkpoints and open image snapshots are protected. Candidate initialization disk ceiling is min(user ceiling, about1% of currently free space, space remaining after safety headroom), initially capped at512MiB mobile /2GiB desktop; no mandatory minimum forces allocation on a nearly full drive.

Runtime boundaries: pinned Coil3.2.0 MemoryCache/DiskCache maxSize are read-only; memory trimToSize can reclaim rebuildable entries, but disk ceiling changes need safe initialization/next startup, never two DiskCache owners or repeated SingletonImageLoader replacement. Android34+ no longer sends some old running-low-memory trim levels, so an eventual controller must use actual process/memory information plus valid thermal/power events; iOS uses native power/thermal state. There is no verified cross-platform presented-frame telemetry here: frame-clock callbacks cannot be reported as actual FPS. These limits are part of the design rather than fabricated automatic optimization.

Primary references: [RFC9110 If-Range/ranges](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-if-range), [Android long-running workers](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/persistent/how-to/long-running), [Android foreground-service timeouts](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/timeout), and agent-reviewed fixed [Coil3.2 MemoryCache](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.2.0/coil-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/memory/MemoryCache.kt), [DiskCache](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.2.0/coil-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/disk/DiskCache.kt), [EventListener](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.2.0/coil-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/EventListener.kt). Reuse the existing downloader, Ktor/Okio storage, WorkManager, reader controls and shared styles; no new dependency or download framework.

### ROUTING-DETECT-20261114 · network design, implementation remains OPEN

Current-thread user requirement (exact message ID unavailable): “以及对于网络相关我希望其实就是直连和代理吗代理分为外面的代理软件但得让用户给他配置成这个软件走全局是不是？以及代理地址配置这样？然后我们做个按键自动检测来帮用户配置好最佳的”. This refines, and does not close, existing ROUTING-DESIGN-142. No transport adapter, route setting or diagnostic button is shipped in this batch.

Use one progressively disclosed “连接方式” row: “跟随系统” (default), “应用直连”, “指定代理”. Following the system means the actual OS route; an external proxy needs MangaFlow included in its applicable per-app/rule route, not necessarily device-wide global mode. Application-direct bypasses an application-layer proxy only; a system VPN/TUN can still intercept it, and lockdown can forbid bypass. Do not claim to rewrite external Clash rules or system VPN policy. Specified-proxy configuration exposes only protocols supported by each real platform adapter, its endpoint and optional credentials through secure storage. No inert protocol choices or unsupported native-channel success states.

Keep one application default. Download/task details disclose an “继承默认” override only when requested; catalogue/images, offline chapters, fonts/models/extensions/components/updates and native Steam/JM must each map to their actual transport before claiming coverage. Preserve source headers, Range encoding/validators, writer generations and publication guards. Routing changes apply to future admissions; an in-flight visible image or download checkpoint retains its original client identity.

One explicit “检测并推荐” action considers only configured/available paths; no arbitrary localhost port scan, discovery of private network services or invented proxy endpoint. Issue bounded, anonymous requests to relevant public service endpoints without account credentials; validate the expected response, distinguishing403/429/challenge responses from transport failure. Compare reachability, first-byte latency and repeatability; a small probe does not measure full throughput or prove a globally best route. Candidate limits are two parallel paths, short timeouts and small traffic, subject to later calibration; subsequent actual transfers feed any adaptive tuning. Results show the recommended route and concise evidence/error. A separate “应用建议” action saves the selected scope, preserving manual choices until the user opts in. Never silently change another proxy application's global settings.

Product wording should say “当前来源推荐连接”, not imply knowledge of every VPN/system setting. Missing native-adapter observability keeps an explicit unsupported state. Implementation order: shared route model and actual platform/native adapters, then route-aware task identity and settings, then bounded diagnosis/recommendation UI. This batch delivers the design only.

Primary platform reference: [Android VPN guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/connectivity/vpn) and [VpnService.Builder](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/net/VpnService.Builder) for per-app routing and VPN bypass constraints.

Evidence/scope: source inspection and separate bounded protocol/cancellation review only. Root combines seven loading/download source files, chapter-history projection and two reader recovery files into one latest-main lease-protected batch, preserving concurrent comments, source/Steam/font/high-refresh changes. No tests, local files/commands/builds, benchmark, user-device/service probes or additional release gate. Keep current workflows/signing/current-main protections; CI trigger, completed build and installed behavior remain separate evidence. Source implementation does not close actual latency, background reliability, battery use or visual acceptance.

### ROUTING-DESIGN-142: every download has an effective route, without a fake VPN bypass

**Recommended interaction.** Settings → 网络与下载 owns the application default, configured proxy endpoints and a progressive “按下载类型设置” list. Default is system. Each download/prepare surface exposes one compact “线路 · 跟随默认（系统）” action; its menu can inherit, use the system path, bypass app/system HTTP proxy, or select a configured proxy. Keep task actions and real byte progress together; do not add an equal-weight card or a new settings dialog at every download click. Show the effective selection and unsupported/blocked status. Local URI imports have no network choice; PC reception says “局域网”.

| Route mode | User-visible meaning and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| 系统网络 | Use the supported platform's current system proxy/network behavior. This is not guaranteed direct access. |
| 应用直连 | Do not use the application or system HTTP/SOCKS proxy for this transfer. It can still traverse an external VPN/TUN/router. |
| 指定代理 | Use the explicitly selected HTTP/SOCKS endpoint through the real transport adapter; do not silently fall back to direct. |
| Inherit | The effective route is task override > category default > application default. Show the resolved result beside the inherited label. |

All category defaults initially inherit; avoid asking users to configure every type. Categories must cover manga originals (including the separate JM path), Steam wallpaper media, images/video downloads, fonts, AI models/runtime/Steam components, application updates (full and incremental), extension/repository downloads, and WebDAV transfers. Browsing/auth/control traffic follows its own clearly documented source/session setting rather than changing implicitly when a large-file task changes route.

For a truly usable external-proxy combination, where the external client supports both application exclusion and a local HTTP/SOCKS listener, provide setup guidance: exclude MangaFlow from that client's VPN/TUN capture, configure its local proxy endpoint once in MangaFlow, then send only the selected tasks to that endpoint. Direct tasks can then use the ordinary network, while proxied tasks deliberately enter the external client's listener. This is a conditional integration design, not a universal bypass capability or an automatically detected/verified setup. Do not guess the user's listener port or modify their external proxy app.

“绕过外部 VPN” is a separate advanced capability, not the definition of DIRECT. Android's VPN owner must allow bypass; bind only the current transfer's socket and DNS when supported. Never change the app-wide process network to satisfy one task. Always-on/blocked-outside-VPN or unsupported configurations report that direct bypass is unavailable. Windows TUN/force-tunnel routes likewise are not bypassed by NO_PROXY. Offer relevant external split-routing guidance rather than show a false success indicator.

**Transfer consistency.** Snapshot the resolved route, endpoint credentials reference and capability when a task starts; keep metadata, redirects, chunks and Range requests on it. New defaults affect new tasks. Existing transfers offer explicit “切换线路并重试”; preserve only the verified resume behavior of that actual downloader, not invented Steam Legacy resume. Proxy failure stays on the selected route; user chooses another route explicitly. Keep route-specific pools and cancellation owners separate from reading/auth jobs. Store endpoint credentials in the existing secret store, not URLs/logs/history.

Actual source audit at c234a9a1:

| Adapter that must be implemented | Current exact path |
| --- | --- |
| Shared Ktor | net/Http.kt + platform Http actuals; ordinary DownloadPageTransfer, FontStore, PanelModelStore, WebDavBackupStore, full nonAndroid updates. There is currently no application proxy policy. |
| JM | DownloadStore decryptedJmPageBytes → JmPlatform.jvm.kt / JmApiClient.fetchImageBytes; cannot assume it uses the ordinary page client. |
| Optional Android components | reader/panels/PanelRuntimeStore.kt independent OkHttp, including SteamWallpaper.android's component loader. |
| Android and desktop incremental update | UpdateManager.android.kt HttpURLConnection; NativeIncrementalUpdate.desktop.kt Update4j openDownloadStream/officialConnection. Only nonAndroid full package uses the shared client. |
| Third-party source install and JS | SourcePluginStore.android.kt and JavascriptSourceRuntime.android.kt have explicit NO_PROXY and validated public DNS/IP ownership. Do not simply remove NO_PROXY: a proxy's independent DNS resolution can bypass the current address validation. Preserve that policy in a bounded compatible adapter or expose honest unsupported status. |
| Native Steam media / CM | Pinned tapline-rt-tokio/src/tls.rs directly TcpStream::connects; HTTP, CM list and CM WebSocket ultimately use it. Shared::new privately builds its HTTP client; Kotlin proxy settings or HTTP_PROXY do not configure this path. Needs a bounded upstream connector extension covering CM/CDN/DNS before “specified proxy” can be offered as working. |
| Local PC/import | WallpaperPc.android already binds owned LAN sockets; preserve that path. WallpaperStore local import has no download route. |

Primary references actually inspected: Android VpnService.Builder allowBypass (https://developer.android.com/reference/android/net/VpnService.Builder), Android Network API (https://developer.android.com/reference/android/net/Network), Microsoft VPN routing (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/vpn/vpn-routing), Ktor3.6.1 proxy support (https://ktor.io/docs/client-proxy.html), tapline f541366 session.rs / shared.rs and tapline-rt-tokio TLS connector. Ktor's current Darwin HTTPS-over-HTTP-proxy limitation must remain visible in platform capability handling; do not promise identical proxy transports on all targets.

Delivery: cloud/in-memory source integration only, one complete latest-main batch with an expected-head lease; keep all concurrent comment/detail/font/source/desktop changes and normal CI guards. No tests/local build/device/browser/account probes, no new review/approval gate. Source auth/UI is implemented; compiled/native/login/installed visuals remain pending normal CI and user feedback. ROUTING-DESIGN-142 is design complete with the above actual transport gaps still OPEN.

## TYPE-86 · typography design candidates · 2026-11-14

User: “关于我们漫画软件的字体系统得好好设计下才行”. Current source inspection: Theme.kt binds most roles to generic SansSerif; no bundled TTF/OTF assets exist in the inspected main tree. The shared metric style already uses Medium and tnum, so this is not a missing-number-helper diagnosis. Page overrides still introduce extra sizes; compact metrics default to10.5sp, their denominator uses .74 of the value size, and heat fits narrow space by further shrinking without a readable lower bound. These are source observations, not new-device visual acceptance.

Candidate families, not approved replacements:
- MiSans: preferred visual candidate for one coherent Chinese/Latin/numeric UI family; comparatively soft contemporary character is a design judgment to evaluate in real samples. Official https://hyperos.mi.com/font/en/ and https://hyperos.mi.com/font/download . Its own license applies; free commercial use is not equivalent to OFL. Do not add the whole Global family or redistribute a standalone font pack.
- Noto Sans SC: neutral comparison candidate with region-specific/variable distributions; preserve Chinese locale and fallback for unsupported traditional/Japanese/rare characters. Official format guide https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk/blob/main/Sans/README.md . Check the exact selected file/license and actual package size before adoption.
- Existing platform sans: lowest bundle growth alternative; shared roles still apply but cross-platform glyphs/metrics differ.
- Inter is only an optional comparison for numeric rows, not a second default body family. Author documentation https://rsms.me/inter/ confirms tabular numbers. Do not use a monospace face for all prose or force tabular figures into editorial titles.

Proposed phone baseline (fontSize/lineHeight in sp; values are this project's candidates):
| Role | Size / line height | Weight | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Work hero title |24 /32|600|Detail/featured work title; content wraps, never auto-shrink to fit |
| Section/settings title |16 /24|500|Section title and settings primary text |
| Work/chapter/control label |14 /20|500|Grid book title, chapter label, navigation and action |
| Reading prose |16 /26|400|Comments and expanded long introduction |
| Compact prose |14 /22|400|Short introduction and ordinary secondary content |
| Metadata/tag/compact metric |12 /18|400 text;500 numeric|Author/update/count/tags; primary content must not be reduced to this role |
| Expanded metric |20 /26|500|Rating detail; denominator/units remain readable and baseline-aligned |

Apply one chosen family to Chinese, Latin and digits first; keep only400/500/600 weights. Same roles reuse the same definitions across recommendation/ranking/updates/library/history/detail/settings/reader. Chinese labels retain normal tracking; negative headline tracking is not copied wholesale from Latin display type. No fixed box may crop larger system text. Controls keep their safe tap area even when labels are compact.

Scores/heat/pages/time/download progress share numeric shapes, decimal precision appropriate to each source and baseline alignment. Use tabular digits for changing values/aligned rows, not merely to change all chapter titles. Default compact numbers never shrink below12sp; fit by preserving the heat and disclosing overflowing source marks using the existing stack, with full values in details. The denominator and万/亿 units are supporting information, not microscopic decorative text. Keep source-native scoring scales.

Artwork/glass text gets sufficient local background contrast, not Thin weight or progressively faded body text. Larger font settings cause wrapping/fewer grid columns rather than manual scale clamps. Package decision must compare actual selected font bytes, keep offline first-launch text available and system fallback, and not require Google Play Services to render text.

Reference floor: the existing Michael Filipiuk fewer-sizes-and-weights principle; Noto format guide; Inter author numeral documentation; Android Compose font and paragraph docs. This section is a design proposal; no font asset/token/page replacement has been shipped or visually accepted in this batch. Font-family selection still needs comparable actual Chinese samples before migration.

## Reader flow, source pressure and offline versions · 2026-11-13 (READING-FLOW-26; device/service acceptance pending)

Current user request: “增加一个下滑回上一话的功能以及我问个问题现在缓存压力加载速度压力是不是更大了这么多源，以及我需要把那个智能分镜功能关闭隐藏掉先”; “现在标签搜索一直出不了结果我怀疑和你的多源有关以及现在多源了那个下载是不是也得改改”, followed by “继续” and “？”. Exact message IDs are unavailable. Preserve the concurrent `89bdaf3` federation/source-row/source-resume changes and `9eb59ca` shared foundation.

- **26A / previous chapter:** in vertical reading, a new downward pull starting at the real chapter beginning uses the existing AndroidX-derived edge physics in reverse: 96dp physical threshold, resistance, hysteresis, release/cancel semantics, reduced motion and one semantic threshold event. The first image must be loaded and its natural height committed; restoration, ordinary downward scrolling from interior pages, flings and cancelled/multipointer gestures cannot arm it. Previous/next share one chapter-change guard, stay within the current chapter group and retain real per-chapter saved positions. Reuse the compact chapter footer at the top only while pulling; no new permanent reader panel, zoom or decorative paging haptics. Horizontal paging keeps its existing controls/gestures.
- **26B / temporarily pause panels:** supersede PANEL-01–08's user-facing availability. `PanelReadingAvailable=false` masks even previously enabled per-book/global settings to OFF, hides the settings section and returns from model UI before stores/runtimes initialize. Existing model files, preferences and panel code remain for a later explicit re-enable; ordinary reading does not enter the guided renderer. This is a complete product pause, not merely removing its switch while an old engine remains active.
- **26C / search:** TAG remains a real Copy-category query, distinct from the new federated title search. The reported blanket service failure is not reproduced here. Confirmed gaps are typed TAG text being only a chip filter even on Search, exact-only simplified/traditional matching, and unresolved foreign labels returning no Copy index. Search now commits a recognized tag to the selected real paths, normalized names/common equivalent labels share the actual catalog identifiers, and chip suggestions include that mapping. Only Copy-origin metadata contributes native paths; foreign paths never masquerade as Copy filters. Unknown labels show a selection/error state instead of inventing title results. Tag-index lookup has the shared foreground deadline. Multi-tag intersection, native pagination and source errors stay truthful.
- **26D / pressure:** more sources add metadata/search requests and catalog memory. Existing auto-discovery/background catalog concurrency is two, each source has a 25s budget, retained raw catalogs are capped at96, and image manifests already have a bounded 32-entry/60s cache. Automatic source discovery does not fetch every source's body images. Add 64 bounded source/query/page search results with a five-minute TTL and 60s fresh-directory reuse; fixed 16-way locks coalesce concurrent identical preparation. Domain generations prevent reusing invalidated data, raw replacements clear freshness stamps, and explicit force refresh bypasses TTL. Foreground title search relies on BrowseCache for reuse and bypasses this repository TTL so refresh/retry still reaches the source. These are source-observed limits, not measured RAM/bandwidth/frame-rate improvements; first-time federation still makes additional requests.
- **26E / downloads:** retain qualified chapter storage IDs, canonical work IDs, existing manifest bytes/headers, hashes, queues, pause/retry/delete and local files. Separate logical “some version is offline” presentation from exact selected-ID download eligibility, so downloading A no longer blocks B. Source choice rows can explicitly queue a validated variant and the download list names its source. A foreign canonical work can contain a native Copy chapter ID, so network preparation, reading, prefetch, retries, covers and saved-picture headers use explicit Chapter source ownership via the shared `chapterSourceMangaId`; they never change history/download keys. Preparation uses the foreground timeout and captures the selected work before enqueueing. No automatic bulk downloading of all versions.

Validation is source/diff/whitespace inspection and independent read-only review only. No tests, local build, API probes or device operation; submit to latest main and confirm the existing CI trigger, preserving manual-only Lint, all signing/R8/startup protections and the current shared migration. Actual pull feel, backend TAG results, download/resume correctness and resource use require the replacement artifact and real user operation; source existence is not acceptance.

## Drawer destination handoff · 2026-11-13 (DRAWER-CONTINUITY-17; source correction, device acceptance pending)

User: “现在点侧边栏切换会很卡卡一下才切换”. The current source awaited native drawer.close() before changeSection, so destination composition began only after the close had finished. This is a confirmed serial delay in the implementation, not a frame-time trace or proof that it is the only device bottleneck. This follow-up replaces DRAWER-CONTINUITY-16's close-first destination rule.

- Keep one reference-keyed DrawerAction, immediate menu selection feedback, the native DrawerState/frosted sheet, actual-offset background relationship, saved root positions and existing input gates.
- For a different root destination, commit sectionName and the drawer root-transition marker while the drawer is stationary. The destination's active AnimatedContent entry acknowledges its committed composition after the next frame. Only then begin native close. The close therefore reveals the prepared destination rather than exposing the old page and then starting the new page. Do not wait for network/data completion, preload all roots, add a fixed delay, or start a second full-page entrance.
- Same-section taps close immediately. Reduced-motion requests snap. If detail/reader state takes over while waiting, stop waiting for a root that is no longer active; do not replay a late destination after close.
- Only the matching active root can acknowledge a selection. New actions and normal/deep-link navigation still invalidate old work by identity. Selection commits before drawer exit, so cancelling a later close does not roll back a legitimate already-committed root. Cancellation must not replay an old destination or clear a newer request.
- Independent read-only review found an existing restart race when motion preference changes: the cancelled actor's finally could clear the same request before its replacement starts. Cleanup now requires both matching identity and an active coroutine; the new actor can retain that same request, while native mutation cancellation and real-user gesture behavior remain subject to device acceptance.
- Keep the existing Haze source node stable and all manual scrim/gesture/input ownership. Destination composition is separated from the moving-close phase through an actual composition/frame acknowledgement, rather than moving both jobs into the same click.

## Optional inference components · 2026-11-13 (OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-01–06; source implemented, CI/device acceptance pending)

User: “？这个运行库一定要加吗”, then “都弄成可选下载吧现在太大了”. These follow the verified 0.1.131 package-size finding in APK-SIZE-01 and authorize moving both native inference engines out of the base APK, in addition to the already optional model weights. Preserve all detection choices and traditional offline reading. This replaces the bundled-engine/compression-only decision, rather than removing high-precision or learned-order features.

| ID | Implemented behavior and observable requirement |
| --- | --- |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-01 | The main APK retains small LiteRT/ONNX Java APIs and MangaFlow's compiled adapters, but excludes libtensorflowlite_jni.so, libonnxruntime.so and libonnxruntime4j_jni.so for every ABI. Native binaries are not repackaged under assets or renamed. Existing model weights remain user-requested downloads. Traditional recognition does not download or initialize a native engine. CI inspects the actual APK ZIP and stops publication if these libraries or model weights are still bundled. No exact replacement APK size is claimed before its actual artifact exists. |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-02 | Reader management separates “运行组件” from “模型”. LiteRT serves Nano; one ONNX component serves both Koharu and Inkwell. Download only the running app process's compatible ABI, expose progress/cancel/retry/delete and preserve previous model files. Selecting an unready AI mode gives honest traditional/geometry fallback; component installation updates the current reader's readiness effect. Closing management leaves an explicit download running. Nothing is silently downloaded merely by opening settings or selecting a mode. |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-03 | CI stages the exact pinned LiteRT 1.4.2 and ONNX 1.31.1 AARs, preserving original library bytes and licenses. It emits two engines × four ABIs as deterministic ZIP assets. runtime-catalog.json is a SHA256withRSA envelope signed with the installed APK's same permanent key and contains app/release identity, engine version, ABI, canonical release URL, archive size/hash and each library's name/size/hash. All component assets, catalog, APK and checksums publish together under existing draft/stale-main/tag/immutability guards. Ordinary build artifacts contain unsigned components and are not represented as installable official runtime catalogs. |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-04 | The downloader obtains the catalog only from the current app version's release, verifies its RSA signature against the installed certificate, checks app identity/version, picks the process ABI and validates archive/library SHA256 plus ELF architecture. Only exact declared native names are written as ordinary files into a fresh noBackup private staging directory; ZIP mode/link attributes are not inherited and license members are not extracted. Bounded sizes, HTTPS/closed redirect hosts, duplicate/path checks, synced writes, read-only sealing and atomic directory installation remain mandatory. A signed local receipt and every installed library are reverified on startup, without networking; identical compatible SDK versions/ABIs can be reused after an app update. No public writable/external native path or unverified fallback is allowed. |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-05 | LiteRT 1.4.2 supports same-App-ClassLoader absolute System.load before TensorFlowLite.init; the exact AAR Java initialization contract was statically inspected. ORT 1.31.1's Android branch ignores the desktop native.path/skip properties, so adapt its actual MIT OnnxRuntime.java Android loading branch to the verified immutable absolute directory, core before JNI. Filter the original loader classes from the build-generated API JAR to avoid duplicate types; preserve the rest of the pinned APIs/native signatures. The path is published before native loading. No downloaded DEX/JAR, reflection-based classloader mutation or plugin framework is introduced. Source identities and differences are in third_party/onnxruntime/ADAPTATION.md. |
| OPTIONAL-RUNTIME-06 | Loading is serialized and completes noncancellably once dlopen starts. Cancellation during checksum verification is rethrown, not reported as corruption. Native failures leave traditional reading available and require a fresh process before retry/removal. Android cannot unload these libraries within the same process: removal after a load/partial load records “重启后删除” in noBackup storage without unlinking live files, then deletes before any load during the next process initialization. Pending removal blocks replacement downloads. Existing image quality, original page files, panel cache/progress, Haze, account and reader controls remain. |

Sources actually read: pinned [ORT 1.31.1 OnnxRuntime.java](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/v1.31.1/java/src/main/java/ai/onnxruntime/OnnxRuntime.java), exact official LiteRT 1.4.2 AAR/class initialization metadata and [upstream TensorFlowLite.java](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT/blob/19c67cbdb91f1fe49d0edb4fc85e5da59ef03b29/tflite/java/src/main/java/org/tensorflow/lite/TensorFlowLite.java), Android API-26 native loader source, and Gradle's provider-backed file dependency documentation. The desktop ORT property documentation alone is insufficient for Android. Existing engine/model licenses remain separately identified, and component ZIPs include the applicable original runtime notices.

Scope: build-generated filtered API JAR, native exclusion/staging, optional runtime store, existing model/camera readiness and management, same-signer packaging/publication plus the bounded upstream loader adaptation. Python AST, workflow YAML, embedded shell syntax and source/diff integrity are inspected without running the application or packaging scripts locally. User feedback: “现在怎么久？我滴妈呀 lint 没必要了吧其实” (1000121541.jpg), followed by “100 多 md？你直接把模型塞进去了吗” (1000121542.jpg). - FAST-RELEASE-02 supersedes the mandatory-full-Lint-on-every-push policy in CI-LINT-01. Both existing workflows default to compilation/assembly, with release R8 and existing signing/publication safeguards. Full Lint is retained as the explicit `workflow_dispatch.full_lint` boolean, false by default; its original warning/dependency/error/report configuration and report-presence checks remain effective when selected. `lint.checkReleaseBuilds=false` prevents assembleRelease from reintroducing implicit Lint. No test task is enabled, and no baseline, downgraded diagnostic or successful-Lint claim is introduced for skipped analysis. A manual default run is also fast; a selected full-Lint run still blocks on actual errors.
- APK-SIZE-01: actual release assets are 4,184,374 bytes for 0.1.128 and 164,847,827 bytes for 0.1.131. Read the latter's ZIP directory and native entries without installing/executing the application. It contains no .onnx/.tflite/.safetensors/.pt weights. Native entries total 160,401,764 bytes: arm64-v8a 38,816,608; armeabi-v7a 26,920,928; x86 47,442,828; x86_64 47,221,400. All have ZIP_STORED (uncompressed), mostly ONNX Runtime and LiteRT. Set AGP 9.5 `packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging=true` so the direct-distribution APK compresses these libraries; preserve every ABI, full inference features and the existing signed update-manifest schema. No APK rewriting/re-signing, model bundling, architecture removal or dynamic native-code download. Installation will extract device-appropriate native libraries; do not equate download compression with a guaranteed decrease in installed storage. Measure the replacement artifact before quoting its actual size.
- UPDATE-NETWORK-01: screenshot 1000121540.jpg establishes an UnknownHostException while resolving github.com before the update request reached the server. Map DNS, timeout, connection and TLS failures to short actionable Chinese messages in both checks and downloads; do not print raw English host exceptions. Preserve the previous verified READY state if refresh fails, retaining its install action, and keep the last successful check time unchanged. Existing manual retry, partial-download continuation, canonical update hosts, manifest/APK signatures, SHA256 and version guards remain. This does not repair the phone's DNS or establish a device-side successful update.

References actually read: official AGP 9.5 [JniLibsPackaging](https://developer.android.com/reference/tools/gradle-api/9.5/com/android/build/api/dsl/JniLibsPackaging), its official 9.5.0 sources.jar, [application extractNativeLibs guidance](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/application-element#extractNativeLibs), and [16KB packaging guidance](https://developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes). Use the Gradle DSL only; no extra manifest or legacy bundle property is necessary for this APK-producing AGP 9.5 app. Runtime model files remain private, optional, verified downloads. Scope is two workflow conditions/inputs, the Lint/JNI packaging configuration, update error/state handling and these existing records. Source/diff/artifact inspection and independent read-only review only; no local build, tests, emulator, device automation, runtime/API probes or model execution. Evidence and limits: the current first-party freeSite bundle submits exactly six fields to its own origin's `/api/kb/web/login`; its normal account center reads `/api/v2/web/user/info`. Our former field encoding matched, but the HTTP client/browser session and post-login profile route differed. Neither that difference nor this change establishes the cause of the original 210. An authenticated official account center was actually observed in shared Chrome, including its nonsecret login-username field. The earlier failed username and later successful username differed; this is not a same-account/same-network comparison and is not MangaFlow login success. No credentials or raw authenticated responses are recorded here.

| ID | Implemented behavior | Completion boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACCOUNT-WEBSITE-04 | Replace the copied native password submission with the official HTTPS account-password page inside the existing account screen. A real installed WebView executes the current official encoding, form validation, request, cookies and errors. The desktop route retains the installed engine's real version; only its device classification is adjusted to select the inspected `/web` contract. Small CSS/viewport overrides fit the actual `#loginV2` form to phone width and remove its duplicated website header/footer. No native password capture, saved password, automatic refill/replay, alternative endpoint or separate outward-browser entry. | The source no longer implements its own password encoding/POST. A WebView is still a different environment from desktop Chrome and the official Android App; do not claim their behavior is identical. Current Android form appearance and successful submission are unverified. |
| ACCOUNT-WEBSITE-BRIDGE-04 | Before loading, install AndroidX WebKit 1.14.0's exact-origin WebMessageListener/document-start observer. Only main-frame messages from `https://www.copy4000.com`, the active attempt/document nonce and newest actual POST submission sequence are eligible. The observer filters both original and final login URL, method, HTTP 200, business 200 and bounded token; it never reads request bodies/passwords/Cookies or forwards raw responses. Early XHR readyState observation allows the site's normal successful redirect; the fetch observer clones its response. | A bridge result is only a candidate. Repository session-generation/cancellation checks and a real profile request remain mandatory; no login is inferred from page navigation, token arrival or nickname text. |
| ACCOUNT-WEBSITE-SESSION-04 | Every pane uses a fresh isolated WebKit profile. Clear that profile's cookies, DOM storage, history/cache and WebView on success, close, route exit or app stop. | Interaction / accessibility / quality | SDK hover/focus/press styles and MaterialOnly scaling respond through each native modifier; reduced motion removes decorative responses and snaps container motion. Root providers map Android UI contrast, preserve upstream reduce-transparency/border preferences, use the app's opaque theme fallback and protect frosted readability. Quality is used normally; low-RAM uses Balanced. No idle animation loop, CPU pixel readback or renderer-specific public settings. |

## Motion system v2 implemented · 2026-11-13 (current)

User first requested “去对我们现在的 uiux 动画动效系统进行升级优化先去好好设计下”, then authorized the complete proposed design with “去交给你完全全部落地”. The seven-page `MangaFlow_Motion_Design_20261113.pdf` is the proposal; this section owns the adopted implementation and its limits. Extend MOTION-01–11 and the existing Ovio/beUI/Vaul/Backdrop adaptations, retaining the latest detail/carousel reversals and concurrent PERF-06–09 / GLASS-MATERIAL-04 corrections. No new animation runtime or dependency is introduced.

| ID | Adopted implementation / actual source | Observable acceptance and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M2-01 | ExpandingSearchBar starts icon and shell together. A measured, fixed-width text row requests focus once its visible text region reaches min(96dp, target text width) and its window is focused. Real results retain their own height. IME owns the first back; a later back previews the search shell, with finite foreground exit and existing hidden-input bounds. | Opening does not wait for the former 70ms lead or 90%/98% completion thresholds. Closing/reversing retains one X and restores the original header without an invisible full-width foreground. Keyboard appearance timing itself remains platform-owned. |
| M2-02 | Keep Ovio's independent leading/trailing edges, selected ranges, text weight reservation and per-pane state. Shared pane entries use the navigation spring, soft fades use 200/140ms, and at most six ranking entrants retain 18ms selection-only staggering. Audience press uses the common .94 icon amplitude. | Rapid selection retargets the present geometry; refreshes do not replay the list or reset positions. Existing male/female depth exchange and full period labels remain. |
| M2-03 | Ordinary route and cover entries share k=520, damping=1 navigation physics; navigation opacity is 160/120ms. Keep placement-specific cover identity, image placeholders and saved source positions. | A cache/image response does not retrigger a route or match another placement of the same manga. Existing sharedElement/sharedBounds distinctions remain. |
| M2-04 | MotionBackHandler uses Activity 1.10.1 PredictiveBackHandler. Each AnimatedContent key owns one MotionBackState shared by its handler/drawing and ReaderScreen. System progress maps to <=8% viewport travel, <=3% scale reduction and a bounded corner change. Completion calls the real close action once immediately; cancellation springs back. Signed origin mapping lets a new gesture catch a cancel return from either edge. | No model navigation, chapter switch or save is committed during preview/cancel. Completing uses the retained route exit. During a predictive gesture the ordinary shared-cover overlay is suppressed so it cannot jump into untransformed coordinates; normal buttons/three-button back retain the cover flight. This is a deliberate adaptation of the current root, not a seekable shared-element implementation or claim that the platform lacks one. |
| M2-05 | Reader tools use 180ms, 12dp overlay entrances with existing fixed system insets and release/cancel seek semantics. Measure the actual lower control host, remove its already-accounted navigation inset and pass the real clearance into ChapterEndComments. Navigator/scrub/modal states suppress previews. | Long titles, font scale and actual action rows do not overlap the comment entry. Tool visibility does not resize/scale the manga or change saved page/offset. Preserve the concurrent tiled long-strip reader. |
| M2-06 | BottomPullLoad retains 96dp, genuine pointer release, final-image/base-zoom arbitration, circular geometry and request ownership. A pointer VelocityTracker supplies only bounded release momentum; the existing feedback returns with k=420, damping=.86. Threshold haptics rearm below .88 instead of at every tiny crossing. | A fast fling cannot request a chapter. Multi-touch/cancellation/reversal do not dispatch. Progress still represents actual distance or the real loading state. |
| M2-07 | SwipeToRemove preserves 55% left-drag release commitment, reset-on-submit and existing undo/storage ownership. Regrabbing catches the returning drawing; cancellation returns with bounded velocity. Threshold haptics rearm below .47. BookshelfBook similarly springs an unaccepted/canceled drag to its original slot; the actual trash target alone decides removal. | An immediate undo cannot resurrect a half-swiped row. No deletion waits on an animation callback. Keyed history/favorite exits and placement respect disabled motion. Trash feedback animates only color/icon, keeping the circular drop geometry fixed. |
| M2-08 | Shared press physics retain beUI k=833/damping=.866, with .94 icons and .985 broad surfaces. Extract the already adopted Settings press-stretch thumb into MotionSwitchThumb and reuse it in ReaderToggle: k=300, damping=.72, 18→21dp thumb width. | Full accessible switch rows stay stable; text does not inherit a moving switch thumb's shape. RTL and the saved software palette remain. No extra press transform is added around an existing transformed surface. |
| M2-09 | Retain existing local long-comment/reply/filter disclosures and fixed icon swapping. Source selection uses color feedback without scaling its text; source/filter touch rows are at least 44dp. | Selection does not move adjacent text or replay the feed. Existing source identity, compact translation and real replies stay intact. |
| M2-10 | ChapterEndComments retains stable per-comment flight parameters and passthrough input. Keep <=3 simultaneous bubbles, 3.6–4.4s flight and 1.2–1.6s admission intervals. Static single preview is used for disabled motion/touch exploration; no decorative timer runs in that mode. ## Remaining performance work implemented · 2026-11-13 (current)

User follow-up to the four remaining items: “那赶紧全部落地”. Scope is startup restoration, chapter-first download preparation, isolated download publications and long-strip region decoding. The existing reader gestures, original image indexes, per-chapter history, explicit download intent and latest restored UI remain the acceptance baseline.

| ID | Implementation | Observable acceptance / evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PERF-06 | LibraryStore now opens preferences and parses saved collections/history/settings on IO. A ready/error stream distinguishes unrestored state from an empty library. Early writes are replayed against restored records; reading/settings wait for readiness and the library uses its quiet loading/retry treatment. Backup export/restore and chapter-history reads await the same owner. | Discovery can draw while personal data restores. An early favorite/progress action cannot replace saved data with an empty snapshot. Resume reads the restored chapter/offset and settings. Readiness is not proof of successful disk persistence. |
| PERF-07 | DownloadStore can load one requested manifest through its chapter mutex without waiting for global initialization. The initial file index reads existence/length, then image-header validation and scheduler reconciliation run on IO. Readers validate their requested page; workers prepare only their chapter before transfer. Generation and per-page write versions protect concurrent replacements. | Opening an online/saved chapter does not wait for every downloaded image's bounds to decode. Nonempty files alone never let a new transfer declare completion: all pages must belong to a validated generation. Pause/delete/refresh retain ownership; damaged files retain the existing repair/error flow. Startup verification updates its in-memory index without rewriting every manifest. |
| PERF-08 | Download status is collected in the current detail, reader chapter and mounted chapter dialog, rather than at the application root. The shared store exposes filtered/distinct flows. Progress saves reuse the stable ID order and sort again only for membership/creation-time changes. | Another manga's download does not invalidate the reading/application root. Current progress, chapter marks and download management still update. Initial cached values avoid clearing download marks during subscription handoff. |
| PERF-09 | Long vertical pages over two viewport heights retain their bounded Coil preview and overlay fixed source bands using Telephoto 0.16.0's actual region decoder. Only visible bands plus one adjacent band on either side are composed; original files/cache snapshots stay pinned for that page. The public custom-source adapter translates crop coordinates while the upstream engine owns sampling, EXIF and decoder pooling. | Detailed regions use cached/downloaded original bytes with no second GET or extra disk copy. Bands remain inside the original page item, keep its fitted aspect/offset/count, and add no touch gesture owner. Unsupported region formats or evicted cache files retain the existing preview. Source geometry/resource review is not measured phone smoothness or visual acceptance. |

Implementation source map: `third_party/telephoto/ADAPTATION.md`. Source/diff review plus independent read-only review covered startup writes, lazy restoration, worker error handling and premature completion. No tests, benchmarks, local builds, API probes, simulator or device automation were run. Deliver directly on latest main, confirm CI triggered, and leave real-device acceptance to the user.

Long menus/panels diffuse more and refract less than small controls. | Retain backdrop colour/structure without a coordinate-based inner white plate. Storage sizing is an estimate from the compact metadata shape and SharedPreferences/XML overhead: typical per-chapter records are a few hundred bytes, so ten thousand chapters are generally on the order of a few MB (titles/IDs/platform overhead vary). The previous per-chapter positions already consume part of that; this change mainly adds names/time and access to them. This is not a measured device-storage benchmark. Actual image caches/downloads remain separate.

## Vertical reader scroll repair · 2026-11-12

User feedback: “看漫画设置成纵向滑动总是卡手”. Recorded from this conversation; no message ID or exact feedback timestamp was supplied.

- **READER-SCROLL-01 — Give ordinary vertical drags to the reading list.** Use Telephoto's `ContentScale.Fit` inside the existing aspect-ratio item, keeping top alignment and the existing pinch/double-tap zoom. `FillWidth` could leave the original image slightly taller than the rounded item, particularly when the item's ratio came from a rounded preview. Telephoto 0.16.0 accepts that small pan range and can consume the rest of the drag after reaching its edge. The reference is the pinned `saket/telephoto` commit `2a5e5f502605367c0f497bbbdc3804a15f5e2f74`, `RealZoomableState.canConsumePanChange`, `internal/contentPlacement.kt` and `internal/transformable.kt`; this is a source-based explanation, not device profiling.
- **READER-SCROLL-02 — Keep image geometry stable during scrolling.** Read original dimensions, including EXIF rotation, from an existing local file or Coil disk snapshot on IO. The bounded adjacent-page prefetch records these dimensions before the image enters the list; reuse them for layout and page recycling. If a visible image's size arrives late, apply the height change only after the drag/fling ends. Preview dimensions remain a fallback when original bytes cannot be inspected. No extra network request, bitmap allocation for measurement, automatic download or separate image cache is introduced. The explicit ExifInterface 1.4.1 dependency matches the version already used by Telephoto 0.16.0.
- **READER-SCROLL-03 — Do not wait for download persistence on the UI thread.** Move reading-page priority updates to IO with cancellation checked after obtaining the store lock. ## Floating search and liquid surfaces · 2026-11-12

Latest feedback: “点击后图标会有一些动画然后搜索框从图标左侧展出”. The input now reveals leftward from the fixed search icon within the existing 52dp toolbar, replacing the former large input panel below it. Keep the drawer visible; the search surface temporarily covers tabs/history and gates their pointer, focus and accessibility access. Use the shared press/transition roles for the small icon response and horizontal reveal. Text and hit targets do not stretch, closing reverses the same path, rapid toggles retarget the current animation, and reduced motion reaches the same usable states immediately.

Only a nonblank query opens the compact results overlay below the toolbar; an empty query has no large card. Query changes never replace, resize or scroll the retained browse content, and only the results overlay receives keyboard insets. Preserve the ViewModel background across configuration changes and separate per-query list positions. Retain input/result content until exit completes, while releasing focus and keyboard ownership immediately on dismissal or leaving the active route. Back, the surrounding scrim and the toolbar close action dismiss search; blank result-panel space must not trigger the scrim. Preserve the full-width carousel from `35217b8` and the shared motion from `112a2fe`.

`LiquidGlassSurface` shares the existing Haze 1.6.0 source/effect pair across search, artwork information and floating artwork controls. It samples the actual background, applies 12dp blur and theme tint, and adds a quiet highlight and rounded edge. Android 13+ refracts only the rim through an original AGSL shader. The shader is compiled once per surface, with dimensions passed as uniforms. Text and icons remain outside that optical layer. Android 12 retains blur; older devices retain a readable tinted surface. Glass on toolbar controls fades with header collapse, while the ordinary toolbar surface appears.

API references checked against the pinned dependency: Haze 1.6.0 usage（`https://github.com/chrisbanes/haze/blob/1.6.0/docs/usage.md`）, effect scope（`https://github.com/chrisbanes/haze/blob/1.6.0/haze/src/commonMain/kotlin/dev/chrisbanes/haze/HazeChild.kt`） and Android AGSL（`https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/graphics/agsl/using-agsl`）. No dependency upgrade, API request or storage migration is part of this change. Source review and the main CI trigger do not establish visual acceptance or device smoothness.

## Default route versus explicit category choice · 2026-11-17

User (Sentinel_46e12f4a0754819183c1948f4f0c96f4): “bug 一大堆默认线路是什么他妈东西我们按类型针对每种设置了不一样的后，切换了默认线路后就又全部重置了”. Screenshot 1000121982.jpg shows Network & downloads → Connection with the default Direct/Proxy selector and a separate Categories tab.

- ROUTE-INHERIT-01: The global default is a fallback, not an apply-to-all command. A category's explicit SYSTEM/DIRECT/PROXY value remains explicit even when equal to the global value. No migration, bulk rewrite, or inferred deletion of existing overrides is permitted.
- ROUTE-INHERIT-02: Reuse the current RouteChoiceRow / Ovio Motion / retained glass popover. Show inherited categories as “默认 · [effective route]”; in their menu only “跟随默认” is selected. Direct/Proxy receive a check only for an explicit selection. Selecting either writes that exact category even when equal to the inherited route. Selecting “跟随默认” removes only that category override. The global heading states its fallback scope. Task-level inheritance stays scoped to the current task, including chapter tasks following the selected manga source.
- Evidence at base 3ea24c7: setDefault writes only the `default` preference; setCategory writes/removes only `category.<name>`. Both backends merge editor changes, and the store serializes writes. Relay reads the complete settings and publishes a rule inventory, without writing route preferences. Auto-check applies a selected batch under a captured-settings identity guard; changes during checking invalidate that result. Periodic automatic optimization can separately update unlocked explicit rules after a fresh verified check. This existing policy and its lock controls are unchanged.
- Confirmed defect: the old menu checked an effective Direct/Proxy value even when no category override existed, and offered no way to return to inheritance. Source inspection has **not reproduced loss of an already-persisted explicit category caused by the default button**; the user's report remains open for installed evidence. No local builds, tests, probes or UI automation were run. Updated UI and persistence behavior are pending actual device feedback; this patch must not be described as a verified data-reset fix.

The owner's latest request removes Copy website authorization and retains only the native password POST login entry. Legacy credentials without identity remain untouched but cannot supply a fabricated synchronization owner; the UI requests password confirmation while preserving local collections/history. ## Next-chapter accepted intent and local recovery · 2026-11-17 (NEXTRECOVER-01–03)
