## Script-session next-chapter recovery · 2026-11-17

- NEXTRECOVER-EPOCH-01: Script image-session replacement now publishes a non-secret process-local revision. Page-manifest cache lookup, in-flight sharing, publication and await return are revision-fenced; repository code reads the StateFlow value without acquiring the script image lock, preserving package/repository lock ordering. Existing per-image opaque epoch checks remain authoritative. No cookie, header or account name is emitted.
- NEXTRECOVER-EPOCH-02: Only an already accepted exact visible current/next chapter intent may resume after its JS source session changes. Replacement waits for retiring jobs and repeats owner, installed-source and immediate same-group successor checks. At most two automatic epoch restarts belong to one accepted intent, not to each epoch; script preference writes cannot create an unbounded retry loop. Exhaustion clears old readiness and reports temporary suspension; reopening the chapter creates a new intent. Network failures do not trigger this path.
- NEXTRECOVER-EPOCH-03: This slice emits JS session events only, not native JM account events. It does not claim to repair every current-page refresh flow, every platform, or the user's exact second-chapter failure. No local build, automated test or device verification was performed; independent static review and normal CI remain separate evidence.


## Native JM account-session preparation fence · 2026-11-17

- NEXTRECOVER-JM-01: Android/JVM native JM login and logout publish the same non-secret process-local revision only after committing their in-memory account/session change. Their mutex-owned photo-image metadata is cleared at that boundary. Failed credential persistence before the session assignment does not pretend that the account changed. Page manifests use the existing revision-fenced lookup, sharing, publication and return path.
- NEXTRECOVER-JM-02: Already accepted exact next-chapter intents use the shared two-restart total and all visibility, owner, successor and retiring-job checks. VM current-session validity also checks the captured revision, so anonymous → login → anonymous cannot revive work through an equal anonymous epoch digest. Existing image route/session checks, per-image gates, file leases and byte receipts remain unchanged. No new credential data is published.
- NEXTRECOVER-JM-03: This covers explicit native login/logout, not inferred server-side expiry, every current-page UI refresh or unsupported iOS JM. No local build, automated test, account login or device verification was performed; actual playback/reading performance is not established by static review.


## Native account commit versus cleanup receipt · 2026-11-17

- JM-ACCOUNT-RECEIPT-01: A committed native login owns the replacement client. Failure while closing the old client must not close that replacement or imply rollback. Login/exit cleanup attempts both cookie removal and client closure, preserving primary and suppressed failures. Cancellation remains cancellation, not an invented success.
- JM-ACCOUNT-RECEIPT-02: A typed, fixed-text receipt distinguishes an already committed local login/logout from retiring-client cleanup failure. Both account controls still reread actual account state and display the cleanup warning rather than a generic retry-login error. Cache invalidation is attempted even for this committed-with-warning outcome; credentials are neither cleared from the new account nor logged. The warning recommends app restart, not repeating the account mutation.
- JM-ACCOUNT-RECEIPT-03: Source review of upstream JMComic-Api-Java v1.1.12 (5a7a4bb4870edb512274dc2adeb4f7c157445321, AbstractJmClient.close/cleanupOwnedResources) found handled I/O/interruption but uncaught runtime cleanup paths. This establishes an exceptional control-flow risk, not an observed device failure. No real account action, local build or automated test was performed.

## Native buffering recovery · 2026-11-17

- VIDEO-STALL-01: Android native BUFFERING is observed independently of parser errors. Only a foreground/Picture-in-Picture, play-requested, unsuppressed network player participates; local files, pending native graphics recovery and existing delayed retry jobs are excluded. Pausing, backgrounding, leaving BUFFERING or explicit seeking resets observation.
- VIDEO-STALL-02: Thirty seconds without increases in actual received bytes or buffered position, or any playback-position change, ends the stalled attempt. Traffic progress extends the idle allowance, but a continuous two-minute buffering interval also ends explicitly. This is a recoverable timeout, not a statement that the source is invalid or the device cannot decode. No synthetic percentage/first-frame evidence is published.
- VIDEO-STALL-03: Mark the attempt terminal before stopping ExoPlayer so synchronous callbacks cannot erase ERROR. Existing generation/engine ownership and release reset remain authoritative. Default playback can use the already-verified same-episode recovery chain; explicit source choice remains locked, and automatic recovery off/zero remain respected. The first native failure opens one 45-second candidate-admission recovery window; later failures do not extend it. This does not promise a global 45-second wall-clock playback deadline.
- VIDEO-STALL-04: No local builds or automated tests. Static review is not device/network/PSYREN first-frame acceptance; sources with real slow traffic can still reach the explicit two-minute bound and offer retry.

## Native first-frame and audio-only boundaries · 2026-11-17

- VIDEO-FRAME-01: READY is decoder/buffer readiness, not proof of a rendered video frame. Android records raw discovered video-group presence separately: false requires an observed audio group and no video group, not merely no supported/selected video choice. Audio-only READY displays that fact without fabricating a first-frame acknowledgement; READY-state rebuffering is not hidden behind the waiting-for-frame message; initial OPENING keeps its separate preparation message. Android also publishes native playback suppression, so focus-suppressed READY/play-intent does not count toward stable recovery-budget reset; other platforms keep their existing default. Confirmed audio-only READY, playing and nonbuffering can satisfy the existing continuous 30-second stable-playback recovery reset without claiming a video frame.
- VIDEO-FRAME-02: A local GPU fallback that rebuilt the native engine must not wait forever outside all timeout handling. Its BUFFERING uses the existing progress/time bounds but reports a local native-recovery failure with source recovery disabled. In READY, only that fallback, an actually selected video track, a mounted nonzero rendering container, foreground/PIP, active play intent and no suppression permit a 30-second no-first-frame observation. Pause, seek, background, detachment and state changes reset it. Ordinary READY playback is not subjected to this new local-fallback limit. A delivered black frame is still a genuine frame callback and is not treated as failure.
- VIDEO-FRAME-03: A mounted Compose container is not proof of an OS Surface's validity or visible pixels. The guarded timeout says only that the local fallback did not report its first frame; it does not identify a bad provider, incompatible source, or solved PSYREN playback. Local renderer failures neither switch sources nor enter the provider-failure cooldown ledger. Audio-only native fallback may finish local recovery without claiming a video frame.
- VIDEO-FRAME-04: Keep the independently published CancellationException import fix. No local compilation or automated tests; actual device surface recreation, background/PIP, GPU driver behavior and first-frame delivery remain unverified. This change does not cover ordinary READY-with-no-frame without a prior graphics failure.

## Generic script-host error evidence · 2026-11-17

Source-only audit found two protocol-independent diagnostic losses: JVM/iOS HTTP429 paths threw before returning the envelope and omitted httpStatus, while the runtime recognized the Venera unsupported sentinel but not the existing Mangayomi “Unsupported source host API” sentinel. Preserve429 as a typed status and recognize both host-owned sentinels, producing only fixed safe messages (never the captured API name, URL, request/response data or credential). Existing request limits, Retry-After handling, origin cooldowns, cancellation, redirects, authentication and source capabilities are unchanged; no new retry is scheduled. A generic earlier screenshot cannot establish either issue as its real cause. No site content, credentials, local build or automated test was used.

The runtime also rechecks coroutine activity before classifying a wrapped JavaScript failure and rethrows a captured native CancellationException. A cancelled HTTP operation must not become a user-facing network/parse error merely because the JS boundary wrapped it. Existing finally cleanup remains active.

## Anime discovery and catalog publication ownership · 2026-11-17

- ANIME-DISCOVERY-OWNER-01: Detail-owned discovery takes its title/year/identity evidence from the currently displayed detail after verifying the caller's subject id. An older library/extension readiness continuation may not replace a newer metadata signature with the original search-card snapshot.
- ANIME-DISCOVERY-OWNER-02: Automatic bound-catalog refresh and explicit refresh share one per-source catalog publication token allocated when scheduled, before coroutine/permit waits. Older queued or late reads cannot regain publication rights after a newer refresh. Existing detail generation, restore epoch, provider revision, binding identity, exclusions and manual episode/group choices remain authoritative.
- ANIME-DISCOVERY-OWNER-03: Explicit refresh has a 15-second timeout and publishes LINKED/UNAVAILABLE only while it still owns the exact request; timeout is not an empty catalog or NO_MATCH and leaves the previous catalog intact. LINKED records catalog association, not stream or first-frame health. Metadata/source/episode matching thresholds are unchanged.
- ANIME-DISCOVERY-OWNER-04: This slice does not claim search exhaustiveness: current automatic search uses first-page candidates, some providers lack sufficient year/shared identity, and some source scripts swallow errors into empty lists. Bounded recall pagination is a separate reviewed slice. No local builds, automated tests or claims of device playback acceptance.

## Bounded anime discovery recall pagination · 2026-11-17

- ANIME-RECALL-01: Automatic source recall may inspect at most three pages per title/original-title keyword, only when that provider declares audited pagination support. Keywords are visited round-robin by page so later title pages cannot starve the original-title first page. It stops on a candidate, and stops each keyword on an empty page or a page containing no new source-local id/URL identities. Non-paginating providers still receive only page one. This is bounded recall, not a claim that every result of every source was searched.
- ANIME-RECALL-02: Pages share the existing per-source 15-second outer budget and four-source permit pool; each individual search retains a four-second limit. Do not restart total time or spawn unbounded per-page work. A failed/timed-out search remains UNAVAILABLE when no candidate can be verified, not a definitive NO_MATCH; scripts that swallow failures into empty arrays remain an explicit diagnostic limitation.
- ANIME-RECALL-03: Pagination does not weaken work/year/shared-ID confirmation, season/group contracts, exact episode identity, exclusions or manual selections. Each result must belong to the requested provider; duplicates use exact source-local id and URL, not title alone. Ownership fixes are a prerequisite. No local builds, automated tests or claims of actual playback acceptance.
